Predictive shrinkage of regression coefficients

Source: R/resampling.R
shrink_regcomp.Rd

Shrinks the slopes of one parameter by a common factor c to correct the overfitting of predictions in new data: the heuristic factor c = (LR - df) / LR of van Houwelingen and le Cessie (1990), with LR the likelihood ratio statistic against the model without the parameter's covariates and df its degrees of freedom, or a factor given by the user. The intercept and the other parameters (precision of a beta regression, say) are then re-estimated with the shrunken slopes held fixed. Works for any family (beta regression, GLMs, distributional models) without random effects.

Usage

shrink_regcomp(object, par = NULL, factor = NULL)

Arguments

object

A fitted model (frequentist, no random effects).

par

Parameter whose slopes are shrunk (default the first).

factor

Optional shrinkage factor in (0, 1]; default heuristic.

Value

The fit with shrunken coefficients (without standard errors), with the factor as attribute "shrinkage".

References

van Houwelingen and le Cessie (1990), Predictive value of statistical models. Stat. Med., 9, 1303-1325.

Examples

d <- data.frame(x1 = rnorm(60), x2 = rnorm(60), x3 = rnorm(60))
d$y <- rbeta(60, plogis(0.3 * d$x1) * 10, (1 - plogis(0.3 * d$x1)) * 10)
f <- regcomp(y ~ x1 + x2 + x3, family = "beta", data = d)
attr(shrink_regcomp(f), "shrinkage")
#> [1] 0.8551958
